finding.claim: authorize() is async but not awaited in DELETE /reports/:id. The returned promise is ignored, so the 403 rejection never stops the handler and remove() runs regardless of grants. Any authenticated user can delete any report by id. The rejected promise is also unhandled, which on Node 15+ can crash the process.
finding.source: Authenticated user (any session) sending DELETE /reports/:id with an arbitrary report id

trace.note: authorize(...) called without await or return; the thrown 403 becomes an unhandled rejection

finding.guards_checked: authorize() checks grants correctly and does throw, but its result is not awaited. No other middleware enforces authorization. The PUT route awaits it, which shows the intent. Session middleware only sets req.user.

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:9-16 throws a 403 on missing grant, but the DELETE handler calls it without await at server.js:20, so nothing stops the handler. The session middleware at server.js:4-7 only sets req.user and enforces nothing. No other middleware exists.
verdict.reason: server.js:20 calls the async authorize() as a bare statement, so its rejection (thrown at server.js:13) is discarded and db.reports.remove runs at server.js:21 for any user. This is unlike the PUT route at server.js:27, which awaits it. The caller only needs a session, and a missing session would throw at server.js:5.

finding.claim: Mass assignment in PUT /reports/:id. The raw request body is passed to db.reports.update, so a caller with write grant on one report can set protected fields such as owner_id or tenant_id, and can also set id, which may let them reassign or take over the report.
finding.source: req.body JSON from a user with write grant on a report

trace.note: whole body passed to update with no field allowlist

finding.guards_checked: No field allowlist or schema validation is visible. The db layer is not in the repo, so it may filter fields, which I could not check. Write permission is required, so the impact is limited to privileged fields.

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:9-16 throws 403 and is correctly awaited at line 27, so it requires a 'write' grant, but it does no field filtering. There is no allowlist or schema validation on req.body, and the db layer is not in the repo.
verdict.reason: server.js:28 passes the unfiltered req.body to db.reports.update after only a write-grant check at line 27, so a low-privilege writer can send owner_id, tenant_id or id. I could not check whether the db layer filters these fields, but nothing visible in the repo blocks it.
